tagline: Plantation houses and a cemetery within a preserved Civil War battlefield
intro: The Averasboro Battlefield Scenic Byway appears in North Carolina’s scenic-byway guide, in a region where NC 82 links Godwin and Erwin. The battlefield district encompasses rural agricultural land, Oak Grove and Lebanon plantation houses, and Chicora Cemetery.

In March 1865, Union troops under Henry W. Slocum crossed the Cape Fear River at Fayetteville and marched up the Raleigh plank road. Near Averasborough they met William J. Hardee’s Confederate corps. On March 16, Union reinforcements helped drive back two Confederate lines, but a third held. Hardee withdrew as more Union troops arrived, leaving his force outnumbered and in danger of being flanked.

For a northbound approach, NC 82 runs from its US 301 junction in Godwin toward Erwin. The battlefield includes Oak Grove, where fighting took place, and Lebanon, which served as a hospital. Chicora Cemetery is part of the battlefield museum, founded in 1994.

moments.title: Oak Grove
moments.text: The Battle of Averasborough was fought on the grounds of Oak Grove, a former plantation of the John Smith family. The house was built about 1764, a two-story Georgian frame dwelling with a full-width front porch and shed-roofed wings.

moments.title: Lebanon Plantation
moments.text: Lebanon served as a hospital when the Battle of Averasboro took place in its immediate vicinity on March 16, 1865. Built about 1824, the plantation house has two stories and a one-story wing. Its weatherboard walls rest on a brick foundation, and a two-tier porch spans three bays of the front. Lebanon and Oak Grove are both included in the larger battlefield historic district.

moments.title: Chicora Civil War Cemetery
moments.text: Chicora’s restored cemetery is part of the Averasboro Battlefield and Museum. The Averasboro Battlefield Commission founded the museum in 1994 on the battlefield. The cemetery also belongs to the battlefield historic district, listed on the National Register in 2001. The battle commemorated here preceded Bentonville by three days.
